rules.statement: Don't report the closure and delegate that a lambda capturing its arguments allocates on each call unless a measurement shows allocation pressure on that path.
rules.why: The maintainer declined this finding: no measurement showed a cost, the cost is small next to a provider's round trip, and the finding itself advised leaving it until profiling shows otherwise.
rules.check: Before raising a per-call closure allocation, look for a benchmark, profile or hot-path evidence in the PR or issue; without it, don't report.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a private constructor to become a primary constructor when the type keeps it private so that a validating static factory such as `Create` is the only way to build it.
rules.why: A primary constructor takes the type's accessibility and can't be private, so it would let any code in the assembly build the type without validation.
rules.check: Before reporting a classic constructor under the primary-constructor convention, check whether it is private and whether a static factory that validates is the only caller; if so, don't report.

rules.statement: Don't ask a dedicated exception type that reports invalid configuration to derive from `InvalidOperationException` unless the repository's instruction files or decision records require it.
rules.why: No convention requires it, and the dedicated type is what callers catch to read its failure details, as the design record names it.
rules.check: Before reporting an exception's base type, look for a rule in the instruction files or ADRs that requires the base type; if there is none and the type is documented as the one callers catch, don't report.

rules.statement: In a test project, don't ask for a shared base test class when each test class already creates its mocks from one strict `MockRepository` and verifies it when it is disposed.
rules.why: The test convention only requires one repository per test class that is verified on dispose. A base-class sample in the conventions shows one way to do that and is not a requirement.
rules.check: Check that each test class owns a `MockRepository` and calls `VerifyAll` or `Verify` in `Dispose`; if it does, don't report the missing base class.

rules.statement: Don't report an internal type for sitting in a folder-matching sub-namespace that differs from its public contract's shallow namespace.
rules.why: Internal types live in a namespace that matches their folder, while a library's public types stay in its shallow public namespace, so a contract and its internal default implementation can be in different namespaces.
rules.check: Before raising a namespace mismatch between a contract and its implementation, check whether the implementation is internal and its namespace matches its folder; if so, don't report.

rules.statement: Don't report a violation of a convention or instruction file unless that file and rule actually exist in the repository under review.
rules.why: The maintainer declined a naming finding that cited instruction files and a rule the repository doesn't have.
rules.check: Before citing a rule, confirm the instruction file exists in this repository's `.github/instructions` or docs and contains that rule; if it doesn't, drop the finding.

rules.statement: In a test project, when several tests check different refusals that throw the same exception type with the same `ParamName`, give each refusal its own message and assert that exact message in each test.
rules.why: If the tests assert only the shared `ParamName`, they all still pass when one check starts refusing another check's input.
rules.check: Look for sibling tests of different validation paths that assert only the exception type or `ParamName` and never the message.

rules.statement: In a test project, use the shared test fixture or helper for setup it already provides instead of rebuilding that setup inline or keeping a private copy of the helper, and factor setup that two helpers repeat into one private helper.
rules.why: Copied setup and duplicate helpers can drift away from the shared fixture.
rules.check: Look for test setup or private helpers that repeat what an existing shared test helper does, or for two helpers that differ in only one argument.

rules.statement: When recording an operation's outcome in telemetry, record `canceled` for an `OperationCanceledException` only when the caller's own token was canceled; record any other cancellation, such as a provider timeout, as a failure with the exception type as `error.type`.
rules.why: Otherwise timeouts are left out of the failure outcome and `error.type`, so failure-rate alerts miss them.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks or outcome mapping that treat every `OperationCanceledException` as canceled without checking `cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested`.

rules.statement: Don't call `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` in `Dispose` or `DisposeAsync` of a type that declares no finalizer, unless an analyzer in the build requires it.
rules.why: The call does nothing there and leads readers to think a finalizer exists.
rules.check: Look for `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` in a type that has no `~TypeName()` finalizer.

rules.statement: A doc comment that describes a relaxation or special case must name exactly the cases it covers, not a broader category.
rules.why: An overstated summary leads callers to expect behavior the code doesn't provide, such as a startup failure they didn't expect.
rules.check: Compare doc summaries that describe relaxed or accepted cases with the code that implements them, and look for wording broader than what the code accepts.

rules.statement: Wrap prose lines in Markdown docs at about 120 columns, as the neighbouring docs do.
rules.why: A long line gets reflowed on a later edit, which makes the diff noisy.
rules.check: Look for added Markdown prose lines that run well past 120 columns.
